sections.title: Conclusion
sections.text:
This research aims to improve the precision of theft detection for energy users using a data-driven methodology. 
Using deep learning models, we analyze power usage characteristics at various time scales and exploit the benefits 
of feature extraction. Therefore, we provide an innovative theft detection approach that relies on CNN and 
LSTM. We assessed the model’s performance using established performance criteria such as accuracy, precision, 
F1-score, and recall. Our observation revealed that LSTM classification surpassed CNN and other state-of-arts 
methods. The classifier demonstrated a 97% accuracy rate when assessed on a testing set. When training a 
model, extracting a balanced dataset from the whole training set restricts the model’s biases. It enhances its 
ability to evaluate the performance of the proposed model on an imbalanced dataset. Our goal is to expand our 
methodology to identify real-time power theft instances. We assessed the efficacy of this approach by analyzing 
SGCC consumers’ consumption habits. Additionally, we can verify its suitability across several regions by 
comparing it to datasets from different locales.
